newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate approves export tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate approves export tax bill.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate approved a bill making exports of primary commodities and some semi-manufactured goods exempt from the so-called ICMS export tax, an official said.
The official said the Senate voted 50 to six to approve the measure, which also eliminates the ICMS tax on imports of capital goods and their transportation between states in Brazil.

The bill is due to be signed by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso Friday and will take effect on Monday. A year after taking effect, the exemption will be extended to goods and electric power used in the manufacturing process.

Planning Ministry officials have said exports may grow between six percent and 12 percent as a result of the new legislation. They add that its impact on exports would be the equivalent of a seven percent devaluation.

At Friday's signing ceremony, Cardoso is expected to veto items included in the bill which would prohibit state governments from offering tax discounts to lure private investors. Several small states said the ban would prevent them from competing for investment with more developed regions of the country.
